dehydrated_text:
Eventually, you'll figure it out. It may take a million years or a thousand years. Who knows? But eventually, you'll figure it out. Because the world is infinite.

What's really important to understand is that you have to figure things out by yourself. No one can teach you. I can give you ideas, and Jesus might tell you what he thinks, but ultimately, you must figure it out on your own. And this is why accepting individual responsibility is so hard for people because they don't want to take responsibility.

The problem is that Jesus says there's a spark inside of you, and it's your responsibility to let it grow. If you let it grow, you will bring happiness to the world and yourself. You'll be able to feast with others in heaven. It's hard—really hard—to think for yourself and ignore people around you to learn on your own.

The book "The Brothers Karamazov" by Fyodor Dostoevsky discusses this problem left by Jesus. Jesus came to the world, telling us that freedom is what will enable us to seek the vine of happiness. But this creates anxiety because now you have to think for yourself and go out into the light, even though you might prefer a normal life watching TV every day.

The church tries to solve this by creating an organized religion and fooling people. They teach that Jesus didn't actually say these things and instead worship Satan, who encourages enforcing our will on others. To be good in the world, we need to be evil. These children are naughty; we can tell them that Jesus will make them grow up and stop being naughty one day, but this process involves hurting each other.

Most people won't ever grow up, so the church must pretend to worship Jesus while actually worshipping Satan. They enforce laws on people to ensure peace, making people sheep who need shepherds. The Catholic Church becomes the evil empire, persecuting those who disobey the law so everyone can live in perceived safety and order.

Jesus's teachings leave a huge problem in people's hearts—people want to obey and be told what to do, not think for themselves. If you make people think, they'll feel fear and anxiety. We need to impose order. In this story, the Catholic Church oppresses people until Jesus comes from heaven, curing them and making them happy. But because the church worships Satan, they arrest him.

The grand inquisitor appears before Jesus and they have a conversation where Jesus is called a prisoner.
